newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar trimmed for now, shares gain ground.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar trimmed for now, shares gain ground.

text.p: The dollar put on a further show of strength on Wednesday, although verbal intervention by the German Bundesbank trimmed its sails by the end of the European morning.

The central bank stepped in to curb a steep dollar rise against the mark, knocking down a news agency report that Germany was keen for the U.S. currency to rise some more, thus easing pressure on the German economy.
European bourses, meanwhile, took their cue from Wall Street to move ahead in early business, although they later pared their gains.
A bigger-than-forecast drop in the British jobless total rekindled fears of higher interest rates and sent the London stock market, Europe's busiest, into the minus column after a higher start.
On the bullion market, gold slipped to its lowest fix since April 1993 at $336.90 an ounce.
A surge in the dollar to 34-month highs against the mark and four-year highs against the yen prompted selling by both gold producers and long-term investors fearing still lower prices.
"It is very difficult to pick a floor for this price," one bullion dealer said."There is selling every morning. It is relentless at the moment."
As the U.S. currency rose sharply against the mark, Swiss franc and yen in early business, currency traders reported market concern that central banks might soon step in to cool things off.
The dollar surged to 1.6935 marks, 1.4500 Swiss francs and 124.48 yen, well up from Tuesday's late European levels of 1.6720, 1.4340 and 122.90.
In the event the Bundesbank succeeded in weakening the dollar for the time being with tough talking, saying it did not believe it should keep climbing, rather than actual currency market operations.

A report from the MNSI news agency had said Germany would welcome further dollar strength but the Bundesbank said it continued to support the view of the Group of Seven leading industrial nations that the dollar had already corrected.
"That (G7) statement said the dollar has been corrected and it was made at a rate of 1.65 marks," the Bundesbank said.
Market analysts said the bank had probably capped the dollar for the day but it could rally again after that.
"I think we've seen the highs for the day but I doubt we've even seen the highs for the week," said Peter von Maydell, senior currency economist at UBS.

Currency traders said Wednesday's second leg of the U.S. Treasury's quarterly refunding could give the dollar even more support. Further ahead market players are looking to Thursday's U.S. January retail sales data and Friday's producer prices.
More signs of strength in the world's biggest economy could provide additional fuel to ignite the dollar's rally, contrasting with problems in Germany and Japan, analysts said.

The London stock market, already wary over the impact on British companies of a strong pound, lost initial gains after news that unemployment fell 67,800 in January, more than double what economists had expected. Bonds also slipped.

"The labour market data are strong and while very unlikely to prompt a near-term tightening of policy, they will increase speculation that rates will have to rise immediately after the election," said Jeremy Hawkins, economist at Bank of America.

The Bank of England said on Wednesday it continued to see the need for a moderate tightening of monetary policy. Earlier Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, who ultimately calls the shots, said he disagreed that interest rates should rise in the near term.
The strong dollar helped pushed sterling to fresh 52-month highs against the German currency around 2.7685 marks, versus 2.7480 overnight, before easing back below 2.76.
In Frankfurt, shares opened strongly but then came down from their highs.

French shares also edged back after surging one percent higher within 10 minutes of opening, buoyed by Wall Street's gains, the dollar's strength and rising bond markets. French company sales have also been encouraging analysts to upgrade forecasts.
In New York, the Dow Jones industrial average reversed Monday's weak session, rising 51.57 points on Tuesday to close at 6,858.11.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6835 marks and 123.85 yen, compared with 1.6720 and 122.90 in late trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
London's FTSE-100 index was down 8.9 at 4,295.4.
In Frankfurt, the 30-share DAX index was up 28.73 at 3,216.31. In Paris, the CAC-40 was 20.36 higher at 2,602.45.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $336.90 an ounce, down from its close in London on Tuesday of $339.55. Silver slid to $4.83 from $4.93.
